title: Hosted API at openeye.sh/v1
description: The first release with a hosted inference API, MCP tools that call it, and the website rebuilt on Vercel and Neon. The CLI package is openeye-sh 0.3.0.

changes.text: Hosted inference API at `https://openeye.sh/v1`: `POST /v1/detect` (YOLOv8, 1 credit), `GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/usage`; `/v1/describe` and `/v1/depth` are listed but not enabled on the hosted API yet
`openeye api` now defaults to the hosted API (`https://openeye.sh`), and `openeye serve` exposes the same `/v1` contract locally
MCP server tools for the hosted API: `openeye_api_detect`, `openeye_api_describe`, `openeye_api_models`, `openeye_api_usage` (with `mcp<2` pinned)
`openeye docs` prints a CLI reference generated from the installed commands (`--json` for agents)
Sign in with 1Profile (Google, Microsoft, Apple and GitHub) alongside email and password
Website and dashboard moved off Lovable Cloud and Supabase onto Vercel, Neon Postgres and Better Auth; avatars are stored in Vercel Blob
Fleet control plane ported from Supabase to Neon Postgres and runs on port 8001
OpenEye is licensed under MIT everywhere
Observation Memory saves live agent-loop observations to your account
`openeye serve` allows the openeye.sh dashboard by default (CORS and Chrome Private Network Access)
Model registry checksums, saving inference history from the dashboard, and the fleet per-IP rate limit

title: Version bump (not published)
description: Tagged v0.2.0 in git right after the first PyPI upload. It was never published to PyPI; the next published version is 0.3.0.

changes.text: Internal refactors and broader test coverage across the CLI, API and dashboard

title: First release on PyPI
description: `pipx install openeye-sh`: the OpenEye CLI, local server and MCP server, with the web dashboard at openeye.sh.

changes.text: CLI: `openeye list`, `pull`, `run`, `bench`, `serve`, `watch`, plus `fleet`, `mlops`, `govern`, `agent` and `api` command groups
Model registry: YOLOv8, YOLO26, Depth Anything V2, Grounding DINO, SAM 2, RF-DETR and SmolVLA
`openeye serve`: REST, WebSocket and a browser dashboard, with hosted-API-compatible `/v1` routes
MCP server (`openeye-mcp`) for Claude and other MCP clients
VLM reasoning via OpenRouter and Nebius, governance presets, and MLOps evaluation
PyPI publish workflow

title: Demo login & dependency fix
description: Demo-ready auth bypass for hackathon presentations and missing numpy dependency fix. (Internal milestone, originally labelled v0.5.1; that version was never published.)

changes.text: Demo login mode — "Continue as Demo User" button on the login page bypasses Supabase auth for local demos
Demo session persists across page reloads via `localStorage` and syncs across tabs
`openeye serve` crash due to missing `numpy` dependency — added `numpy>=1.24` to core dependencies in `pyproject.toml`

title: MLOps lifecycle platform
description: Full MLOps pipeline with model registry, A/B testing, retraining, batch inference, and shadow deployments. (Internal milestone, originally labelled v0.5.0; that version was never published.)

changes.text: Model registry with versioned storage, stage management (dev / staging / production / archived), and format support for ONNX, TorchScript, SafeTensors, TensorRT, and CoreML
A/B testing framework with traffic splitting, statistical comparison (accuracy, latency p95, error rate), and automatic winner detection
Retraining pipelines with configurable triggers (accuracy drift, scheduled cron, manual, data volume) and auto-promotion after validation
Batch inference jobs with S3 / GCS / local storage backends, parallel worker support, and progress tracking with ETA
Benchmark matrix for cross-hardware performance comparison across Jetson, A100, T4, CPU, MPS, and TensorRT targets
Shadow deployments to run candidate models alongside production with agreement rate and divergent sample tracking
Feedback and annotation system for false positives, misclassifications, and bounding box corrections with dataset batching for retraining
Validation test suite with configurable assertions and batch execution across model versions
Model lineage tracking — parent models, dataset versions, code commits, hyperparameters, and training duration
Model export pipeline now supports conversion between ONNX, TensorRT, and CoreML from the dashboard

title: Fleet management
description: Edge fleet control plane with device registration, staged deployments, OTA updates, and real-time monitoring. (Internal milestone, originally labelled v0.4.1; that version was never published.)

changes.text: Fleet control plane backend on port 8001 with device, deployment, heartbeat, command, OTA, alert, maintenance, and group services
Device registration and discovery for cameras, robots, edge nodes, gateways, and drones with hardware spec capture
Device groups with tag-based filtering, auto-scaling policies (CPU threshold, cooldown), and batch operations
Staged model deployments with canary, rolling, blue-green, and all-at-once strategies, plus multi-stage rollout with percentage targets
OTA firmware and model update distribution with checksum verification and bandwidth throttling
Maintenance window scheduling with recurrence rules and device / group targeting
Fleet alerts (device_offline, high_resource_usage, deployment_failed, heartbeat_missed, temperature_high, disk_full) with severity levels and resolution tracking
Device command queue — restart, update_config, deploy_model, rollback, OTA update, and decommission with status tracking
Device agent with heartbeat client, command executor, model cache, bandwidth limiter, resource monitor, and config manager
Fleet dashboard with summary cards, device status table, deployment tracker, and 15-second auto-refresh
CLI fleet commands — `openeye fleet devices`, `openeye fleet deploy`, `openeye fleet groups`, `openeye fleet alerts`, `openeye fleet ota`
Supabase migrations for fleet tables (devices, device_groups, heartbeats, deployments, deployment_device_status, maintenance_windows, fleet_alerts, device_commands) with row-level security
Device registry schema expanded — breaking change for existing device records. Run `openeye fleet migrate` to update.
